name: audit_events
description: Read the Linux audit log (auditd's audit.log and its rotations, gzip allowed) with the standard library and group its records into events by the stamp audit(<seconds>.<fraction>:<serial>). `paths` is an explicit, ORDERED list (oldest first, as the caller names the rotations): the files are streamed in that order, a line over 1 MiB is located (file, line, offset, length) and not parsed, CRLF, NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8 and the ENRICHED format (the interpreted KEY=value pairs after the 0x1d separator) are read, and an event whose records fall on both sides of a rotation is one group (a window of 256 open groups spans the files). Each group carries its first and last file, line and byte offset, the event id, the raw time beside the ISO 8601 UTC one, the node (when the log has node=), the record types in order, per-record locators, the numeric and enumerated fields of the grammar (a fixed list: pid, ppid, the uids and gids, auid, ses, syscall, success, exit, items, arch, tty, res, op, key, the PATH item, inode, dev, mode and nametype, the status counters), EXECVE argc and the byte length of each argument (a split argument, aK_len with aK[0], aK[1], is joined by length and checked against its declared length), the PROCTITLE length and its argument count, the CWD length, the PATH name lengths, the parts that are missing (a PATH short of the SYSCALL's items, EXECVE arguments short of argc, an execve system call of x86_64 or aarch64 with no EXECVE or PROCTITLE record) and the parse errors. An execve's command line, `exe`, `cwd`, a PATH name, `comm`, a typed account name, a host name and every field outside the grammar's list are lengths, never text, and nothing is hashed: the whole of every line is in audit-text.jsonl (mode 0600, created exclusively) only on write_text, which is refused outside a job and in a job that was not run with secret_output: true (declared: a job that sets write_text is run as secret output, and the tool refuses it when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1); a line over the 1 MiB limit is not in that file, its locator is in oversize_lines. An address is shown only where it parses as an IP address. The answer says what auditd's records cannot say: a SYSCALL's success is the system call's result and not the command's, auid 4294967295 is an audit uid that was never set (marked unset), and an absent event is bounded by the rules, the backlog (lost_and_daemon_records lists every record with lost= and every DAEMON_* record) and the rotations the caller collected (rotation_gaps names a rotation number missing from the names given; gaps_between_files and files_out_of_time_order, the seconds between one file's last record and the next file's first). The serial restarts after a reboot or an auditd restart: a serial that falls while time does not is a serial_reset (located), a stamp seen again after its group was closed is a continued_group, and a run of groups whose time is below the highest time seen is a time_regression_run (file, line, seconds backwards). `identity` is a list of passwd and group files OF THE EVIDENCE (at most eight, 8 MiB each): a uid or gid is named from them, listing up to five names an id has, and stays numeric without them; this machine's /etc/passwd and /etc/group are never read. `types` (a record type, or a prefix ending in *) and since/until (a date and time with its zone, Z or +hh:mm, never read in this machine's zone) select the events listed from what is shown; events_total and every count are over all events read, and the filters never look at text the answer withholds. Events are listed up to limit and every event is in the paging file named in pages.events; in a job the answer without its events is also written to receipt.json (a name already there is never replaced). max_seconds (default 120, at most 240, under the manifest's 300) is checked every 256 lines, every block and every file, and a read that reaches it is partial with the file and line where it stopped. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`; all_lines_parsed and all_files_read stay beside them, and a line that is not an audit record, a line over the limit, a damaged or truncated gzip file, a file expanding past 4 GiB or a file not reached in time make the status partial. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP ends the tool with one JSON last word (status failed, exit 128 plus the signal) naming the paging files and the text file it had written, and an unexpected exception ends it with one JSON document and exit 1, never a traceback. A symlink, a non-regular file and a disk image are refused before anything is read. It does not read auditd's configuration or rules, aureport summaries or ausearch output. compare_ausearch: true runs the installed `ausearch` as a second reader on a sample (the first 2000 lines of the first file) and says `agree`, `disagree` or `not_run` in second_reader, with the installed version recorded and the differences counted (records and events found by only one reader) and never their text. It is refused outside a job and in a job that was not run with secret_output: true (declared: a job that sets compare_ausearch is run as secret output), because the sample is a copy of evidence text, written 0600 in a private directory under $OUT and removed afterwards. Before the sample, a one-record probe file must come back through `ausearch -if <file> -r` (the file-input contract, checked on the installed version): if it does not, or no `ausearch` is installed, or the version cannot be read, the result is not_run and says why. `-i` is never passed (it would name users through this machine's passwd and group). The program runs in this tool's own process group, with no stdin, its stderr discarded, a 32 MiB cap on its output and at most 30 seconds, and a deadline, an output past the cap or a SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP ends it and what it started; when compare_ausearch is set, up to 35 seconds of max_seconds are kept for it.  A process that ausearch (compare_ausearch) left running after it exited and that holds its pipes is noticed one second after the program ended (the pipes are let go, however slowly it writes), then stopped, killed and reaped by settle(); the answer is then partial (program_group.left_behind and a line in status_basis (the second reader's result is then not trusted)), because what it wrote into a pipe cannot be told from the program's output. A host where the absence of a leftover cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused) does not make this tool partial, because it reports only what the program printed: program_group.unproven says why. A refusal carries no program_group. A process that is no descendant of the program (started through a service manager) is not found.

paths.description: The audit files in rotation order, oldest first (audit.log.2.gz, audit.log.1, audit.log): up to 1000 regular files of the evidence, read in the order given; a link, a pipe or a disk image is refused

identity.description: Optional: up to eight passwd and group files of the evidence, used to name uids and gids; without them they stay numeric (this machine's own are never read)

types.description: List only events that have a record of one of these types (SYSCALL, EXECVE, USER_*; a trailing * is a prefix); counts stay over every event

since.description: List only events from this instant on: a date and time with its zone, such as 2026-02-14T09:30:00Z or 2026-02-14T11:30:00+02:00 (no zone is refused)

until.description: List only events before this instant: a date and time with its zone (no zone is refused)

limit.description: Events shown inline (default 100); every event listed is in the paging file named in pages.events when there are more

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 120, at most 240): what is left unread is named and the answer is partial

compare_ausearch.description: SENSITIVE: Run the installed ausearch (-if <sample> -r, never -i) on the first 2000 lines of the first file and compare it with this reader: agree, disagree or not_run, differences counted and never shown (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job run with secret_output: true (declared secret_output: a job that sets compare_ausearch is run as secret output)

write_text.description: SENSITIVE: Write every line of the files, whole, with its file, line, offset, event id and record type to $OUT/audit-text.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused (declared secret_output: a job that sets write_text is run as secret output, and the tool refuses write_text when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1)
